subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and what timeout/denial/channel-delivery contract should it use?
rationale: The remaining work changes fallback runtime behavior and adds model-routing config, which repository policy treats as product- and compatibility-sensitive rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design Core Opt-In Gate
options.body: Define a default-off per-agent or per-session approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery semantics, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

options.title: Keep Fallback Automatic
options.body: Treat current fallback notices plus response-prefix attribution as the supported visibility/control model and close the approval-gate direction as not planned.

options.title: Route Through Extension API
options.body: Design a plugin or approval-event extension point first so specialized deployments can own fallback approval policy outside core.

recommendation.title: Design Core Opt-In Gate
recommendation.body: Define a default-off per-agent or per-session approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery semantics, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing candidate from fallback feature history and sampled contribution volume across the affected runtime/config surface.
